rationale:
DECISION. Split root.deformation-a1.onto_skeleton-a1.telescope_limit-a1 (deformation_telescope_limit) into 4 children. All 4 are comparator-accepted declarations, reused by name with byte-identical frozen Lean types, titles and statements, so no new DAG node is created. The selected node keeps its frozen type and its supplied proof route. Its own Lean proof becomes a short inline assembly (below), with no new named helper (problem.md: every new named helper needs its own node).

WHY SPLIT. Without a split, the node may use only its two resolved dependencies, cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le and iwl_cr_support_lemmas. Step 4 of the supplied proof (A′ is a current) would then have to re-derive inline, inside one theorem, everything the flat_iff_weak branch needed five separately accepted nodes for:
- the coefficient-norm comparison |α| ≤ √(N^k)‖α‖ (fiw_ims_sc_covectorNorm_le_opNorm);
- uniform smallness of test forms converging to 0 (fiw_ims_sc_converges_zero_small);
- the continuity criterion (fiw_ims_sc_continuous_of_bound);
- the series bound (fiw_ims_sc_series_bound);
- boundedness of test forms (fiw_ims_sc_testForm_bounded).
The accepted fiw_ims_series_current (root.flat_iff_weak-a1.im_series-a1.series_current-a1, candidate 2065ad1f, comparator passed) packages exactly this content: the series part of Steps 1, 3 and 4, plus the series mass estimate of Steps 5–6 (the A_0 part stays in the assembly). It states that a series Σ c_r T_r of currents in an open U with locally summable masses defines a current S, with HasSum (r ↦ c_r T_r(ω)) (S(ω)) and M_W(S) ≤ Σ' |c_r| M_W(T_r) for every W. This is a genuine reusable obligation: it is exactly the existence of the M-limit in printed (19) (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, p. 166: the sequences are "Cauchy sequences relative to M", hence there are currents Q, S_1, R_1 with lim M(Q − …) = 0), in telescoped form. Reusing it removes the main formalization risk of this node. The run has accepted all-reuse splits made on the merits with the same structure (no new node, assembly kept in the selected node): root.isoperimetric-a1.zero_mass_iff-a1, root.slicing-a1.slice_integer_multiplicity-a1.tau_current-a1, root.slicing-a1.slice_integer_multiplicity-a1.coarea-a1.c1_approx-a1 and root.slicing-a1.slice_integer_multiplicity-a1.coarea-a1.chart_cover-a1 (all accepted, decomposition audits acceptable).

CHILDREN ↔ SUPPLIED PROOF.
- series_current (fiw_ims_series_current, reused). Covers the series part of Step 1 (|B_μ(ω)| ≤ M(B_μ)·sup|ω| gives absolute convergence), Step 3 (linearity of ω ↦ Σ B_μ(ω)), Step 4 (sequential continuity via sup|ω_j| → 0) and the estimate ofReal(Σ_μ B_μ(ω)) ≤ Σ_μ M(B_μ) for admissible ω used in Steps 5–6. It is applied with U = univ, c ≡ 1 and T_r := B_{r+ν}, for each ν.
- series_mass_bound (fiw_ims_mass_bound, reused). The accepted dependency of series_current, mirrored. It is the pointwise bound of Step 1.
- support_lemmas (iwl_cr_support_lemmas, reused). Part (2) is (F3)(2) of the supplied proof and gives Step 7. It is already a resolved dependency of this node; it is repeated as a child so that the children alone imply the selected statement (child/dependency overlaps already occur in accepted nodes, e.g. cone_exists, cone_estimates).
- vanish_off_support (isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support, reused). The accepted dependency of support_lemmas, mirrored.
- Not used: the resolved dependency cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le (F1). Its role (Step 1) is now inside series_current.
- Stays in the selected node: Step 2 (telescoping), the construction A′ := A_0 + S, the identification of each D_ν with a tail series current, and the final sSup argument of Step 6.

ASSEMBLY (inline proof of Submission.deformation_telescope_limit from the children). Let N, k, A, B be given, with hrec: A_{ν+1}(ω) = A_ν(ω) + B_ν(ω) and hfin: Σ'_ν M(B_ν) < ∞.
(a) Tail series currents. Fix ν ∈ ℕ. Apply series_current with P = N, n = k, U = univ (isOpen_univ), T_r := B_{r+ν} and c ≡ 1.
- Its hypothesis holds for every W, using ((1 : ℤ).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) = 1:
  Σ'_r M_W(B_{r+ν}) ≤ Σ'_r M(B_{r+ν})   (massOn_mono with W ⊆ univ; ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum)
  ≤ Σ'_r M(B_r)   (ENNReal.tsum_comp_le_tsum_of_injective, r ↦ r + ν injective)
  < ∞.
- It gives S_ν with HasSum (r ↦ B_{r+ν}(ω)) (S_ν(ω)) for all ω, and M(S_ν) = M_univ(S_ν) ≤ Σ'_r M(B_{r+ν}).
- Put S := S_0. Then HasSum (r ↦ B_r(ω)) (S(ω)) and M(S) ≤ Σ'_r M(B_r).
(b) Telescoping (Step 2). For all i and ω, A_i(ω) = A_0(ω) + Σ_{μ<i} B_μ(ω), by induction on i using hrec and Finset.sum_range_succ.
(c) The limit current (Steps 3–4).
- GeometricCurrentOn has no Add instance (README: linear combinations are written pointwise), so A′ is built by hand: A′ := ⟨A_0.toCurrent + S.toCurrent, continuity⟩.
- Continuity: if TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0, then A_0(ω_j) → 0 and S(ω_j) → 0 by the continuous' fields of A_0 and S, so their sum tends to 0 (Tendsto.add).
- By definition A′(ω) = A_0(ω) + S(ω).
(d) First conjunct (weak convergence). A_i(ω) = A_0(ω) + Σ_{μ<i} B_μ(ω) by (b), and this tends to A_0(ω) + S(ω) = A′(ω) (HasSum.tendsto_sum_nat, tendsto_const_nhds.add). So WeaklyConvergesOn A A′.
(e) Second conjunct (Step 6). A′.mass is the sSup of ofReal(A′(ω)) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k univ. For each such ω:
  ofReal(A_0(ω) + S(ω)) ≤ ofReal(A_0(ω)) + ofReal(S(ω))   (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le)
  ≤ M(A_0) + M(S)   (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn)
  ≤ M(A_0) + Σ'_ν M(B_ν)   (by (a)).
sSup_le then gives A′.mass ≤ M(A_0) + Σ'_ν M(B_ν). This needs no case split on M(A_0) = ∞.
(f) Third conjunct (Step 5). Let ν ∈ ℕ and D_ν with D_ν(ω) = A′(ω) − A_ν(ω) for all ω.
- By (b) and (c), D_ν(ω) = S(ω) − Σ_{μ<ν} B_μ(ω).
- hasSum_nat_add_iff' ν turns HasSum (r ↦ B_r(ω)) (S(ω)) into HasSum (r ↦ B_{r+ν}(ω)) (S(ω) − Σ_{μ<ν} B_μ(ω)).
- Uniqueness of sums (HasSum.unique) and (a) give S_ν(ω) = D_ν(ω) for every ω, so D_ν = S_ν (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
- Hence M(D_ν) = M(S_ν) ≤ Σ'_μ M(B_{μ+ν}).
(g) Fourth conjunct (Step 7). Apply support_lemmas part (2) with P = N, n = k, U = univ (isOpen_univ), K = F, Z_j = A_j and Z = A′, using IsClosed F, spt A_j ⊆ F for all j, and (d).

subproblems.title: Mass bound |X(η)| ≤ M_V(X)·C for test forms with Euclidean coefficient norm ≤ C
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U, V ⊆ ℝ^P arbitrary sets, X ∈ D_k(U) a current (GeometricCurrentOn U k), η ∈ D^k(U) a test form (TestFormOn U k) and C ∈ ℝ with C > 0, tsupport η ⊆ V and covectorEuclideanNorm(η(x)) ≤ C for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then ENNReal.ofReal |X(η)| ≤ M_V(X) · ENNReal.ofReal C in [0, ∞].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (V : Set (Eucl P)) (η : TestFormOn U k) (C : ℝ), 0 < C → tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) ⊆ V → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) x) ≤ C) → ENNReal.ofReal |X η| ≤ X.massOn V * ENNReal.ofReal C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration: this child is DAG node root.flat_iff_weak-a1.im_series-a1.mass_bound-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit bf9ca0af59c29a43051813c46db6cfd1dc1429fe, isolated comparator passed = True, declaration Submission.fiw_ims_mass_bound). It is reused by name with the byte-identical frozen Lean type, title and statement, so no new DAG node is created; its status is an accepted checkpoint (accepted with a candidate commit), which is the controller's condition for cross-branch reuse. Role in the selected parent (root.deformation-a1.onto_skeleton-a1.telescope_limit-a1, deformation_telescope_limit): the estimate ofReal|X(η)| ≤ M_V(X)·ofReal C for test forms η supported in V with Euclidean coefficient norm ≤ C. It is the declared dependency of the reused sibling series_current (fiw_ims_series_current), whose accepted proof calls it 'mass_bound'; it is listed here only to mirror that accepted dependency edge (its role is the pointwise bound |B_ν(ω)| ≤ M(B_ν)·sup|ω| of Step 1 of the supplied proof). The assembly of the selected parent does not invoke it directly. The accepted, independently audited natural-language proof of this exact statement follows verbatim.

Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α for a k-covector α; e_1, …, e_P is the standard basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun).

1. (Homogeneity.) For a ∈ ℝ and a k-covector α, |a • α| = |a|·|α|.
   - (a • α)(v) = a·α(v) for every k-tuple v.
   - So each summand (α(e_{I_1}, …, e_{I_k}))² with I strictly increasing, in the sum under the square root defining covectorEuclideanNorm, is multiplied by a². The other summands are 0.
   - √(a²·s) = |a|·√s for s ≥ 0.

2. (Rescaled forms are admissible.) For s ∈ {1, −1} let η_s := (s·C⁻¹) • η, an element of the submodule TestFormOn U k.
   - Its underlying form is x ↦ s·C⁻¹·η(x), so its support lies in that of η, and tsupport η_s ⊆ tsupport η ⊆ V (tsupport_smul_subset_right).
   - By step 1, |η_s(x)| = C⁻¹·|η(x)| ≤ C⁻¹·C = 1 for every x.
   - Hence η_s ∈ massAdmissibleOn U k V.

3. (Definition of mass.)
   - By GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, ENNReal.ofReal(X(η_s)) ≤ M_V(X).
   - X.toCurrent is ℝ-linear (map_smul), so X(η_s) = s·C⁻¹·X(η).
   - Choose s := 1 if X(η) ≥ 0 and s := −1 otherwise. Then s·X(η) = |X(η)|, so ENNReal.ofReal(C⁻¹·|X(η)|) ≤ M_V(X).

4. (Undo the scaling.) Since C > 0 and C⁻¹·|X(η)| ≥ 0,
   ENNReal.ofReal|X(η)| = ENNReal.ofReal(C⁻¹·|X(η)|·C) = ENNReal.ofReal(C⁻¹·|X(η)|)·ENNReal.ofReal C   (ENNReal.ofReal_mul)
   ≤ M_V(X)·ENNReal.ofReal C   (multiplication is monotone in [0, ∞]). ∎
proof_key_steps: ±C⁻¹η lies in massAdmissibleOn U k V (tsupport ⊆ V, pointwise norm ≤ 1)
le_massOn and linearity give ofReal(C⁻¹|X(η)|) ≤ M_V(X)

subproblems.title: An integer series of currents with locally summable masses defines a current with the mass bound
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T_r ∈ D_n(U) (r ∈ ℕ) arbitrary currents (GeometricCurrentOn U n, not necessarily integer multiplicity) and c_r ∈ ℤ such that Σ'_r |c_r|·M_W(T_r) < ∞ in [0, ∞] for every open W ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContainedOpen W U). Then there is S ∈ D_n(U) such that for every ω ∈ D^n(U) the series Σ_r c_r T_r(ω) has (unconditional) sum S(ω), i.e. HasSum (r ↦ c_r T_r(ω)) (S(ω)), and M_W(S) ≤ Σ'_r |c_r|·M_W(T_r) for every set W ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (T : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n) (c : ℕ → ℤ), (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → (∑' r, ((c r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * (T r).massOn W) < ∞) → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ ω, HasSum (fun r => (c r : ℝ) * T r ω) (S ω)) ∧ ∀ W, S.massOn W ≤ ∑' r, ((c r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * (T r).massOn W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration: this child is DAG node root.flat_iff_weak-a1.im_series-a1.series_current-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 2065ad1fee8c7dc9474c00d6ca127895bd6127f5, isolated comparator passed = True, declaration Submission.fiw_ims_series_current). It is reused by name with the byte-identical frozen Lean type, title and statement, so no new DAG node is created; its status is an accepted checkpoint (accepted with a candidate commit), which is the controller's condition for cross-branch reuse. Role in the selected parent (root.deformation-a1.onto_skeleton-a1.telescope_limit-a1, deformation_telescope_limit): this is the series part of Steps 1, 3 and 4 of the supplied proof, for the series Σ_μ B_μ(ω): absolute convergence from |B_μ(ω)| ≤ M(B_μ)·sup|ω|, linearity of the sum, and sequential continuity from sup|ω_j| → 0 via |α| ≤ √(N^k)‖α‖. It also gives the series mass estimate used in Steps 5 and 6 (ofReal of the sum ≤ Σ masses, then sSup). The A_0 part and the construction A′ := A_0 + S stay in the parent's assembly. The parent applies it with U = univ (open), c ≡ 1 and T_r := B_{r+ν} for every ν ∈ ℕ. For ν = 0 it yields the current S with HasSum (r ↦ B_r(ω)) (S(ω)), from which A′ := A_0 + S is built. For general ν it yields S_ν with HasSum (r ↦ B_{r+ν}(ω)) (S_ν(ω)) and M(S_ν) ≤ Σ'_r M(B_{r+ν}), and every D_ν of the third conjunct equals S_ν by extensionality. In the verbatim proof below, 'mass_bound' denotes the sibling series_mass_bound (fiw_ims_mass_bound). The accepted, independently audited natural-language proof of this exact statement follows verbatim.

Notation:
- |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; ‖α‖ := the operator norm of α as a continuous alternating map.
- |c_r| := ((c_r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) = ENNReal.ofReal|(c_r : ℝ)|.
- A(W) := Σ'_r |c_r|·M_W(T_r) ∈ [0, ∞] for a set W.
- 'mass_bound' is the sibling: ofReal|X(η)| ≤ M_V(X)·ofReal C whenever C > 0, tsupport η ⊆ V and |η(x)| ≤ C for all x.

0. (Auxiliary facts.)
   (a) For every compact K ⊆ U there is W with CompactlyContainedOpen W U and K ⊆ W. Indeed ℝ^P is locally compact and regular, so exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure gives an open W with K ⊆ W, closure W ⊆ U and closure W compact.
   (b) |α| ≤ D·‖α‖ for every n-covector α, where D := √(P^n).
       - For every I : Fin n → Fin P, |α(e_{I_1}, …, e_{I_n})| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖e_{I_i}‖ = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; basis vectors have norm 1).
       - The sum defining |α|² has at most P^n nonzero terms.
   (c) For every ω ∈ D^n(U) there is B_ω ≥ 0 with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B_ω for all x: ω is continuous (smooth) and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport ω, on which it is bounded. By (b), |ω(x)| ≤ D·B_ω for all x.
   (d) Multiplying an inequality a ≤ b in [0, ∞] by |c_r| keeps it valid, also when c_r = 0 (both sides become 0) and when b = ∞.

1. (Absolute summability; definition of S(ω).) Fix ω ∈ D^n(U).
   - K := tsupport ω is compact and K ⊆ U (definition of TestFormOn). By 0(a) there is W ⊂⊂ U with K ⊆ W, and A(W) < ∞ by hypothesis.
   - Put C := D·B_ω + 1 > 0, so |ω(x)| ≤ C for all x.
   - mass_bound with X := T_r, V := W, η := ω gives ofReal|T_r(ω)| ≤ M_W(T_r)·ofReal C.
   - By 0(d), for every r: ofReal|c_r T_r(ω)| = |c_r|·ofReal|T_r(ω)| ≤ ofReal C·|c_r|·M_W(T_r).
   - Hence Σ'_r ofReal|c_r T_r(ω)| ≤ ofReal C·A(W) < ∞ (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum, ENNReal.tsum_mul_left).
   - Nonnegative reals with finite [0, ∞]-valued sum are summable, so r ↦ |c_r T_r(ω)| is summable. As ℝ is complete, r ↦ c_r T_r(ω) is summable.
   - Define S₀(ω) := Σ'_r c_r T_r(ω). Then:
     • HasSum (r ↦ c_r T_r(ω)) (S₀(ω)) (Summable.hasSum);
     • |S₀(ω)| ≤ Σ'_r |c_r T_r(ω)| (norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm);
     • ofReal|S₀(ω)| ≤ Σ'_r ofReal|c_r T_r(ω)| (ENNReal.ofReal_tsum_of_nonneg).

2. (Linearity.) Let ω, η ∈ D^n(U) and a ∈ ℝ.
   - By linearity of each T_r: c_r T_r(ω + η) = c_r T_r(ω) + c_r T_r(η), and c_r T_r(a • ω) = a·(c_r T_r(ω)).
   - HasSum.add and HasSum.mul_left give HasSum (r ↦ c_r T_r(ω + η)) (S₀ω + S₀η) and HasSum (r ↦ c_r T_r(a • ω)) (a·S₀ω).
   - By uniqueness of sums (HasSum.unique together with step 1 for ω + η and a • ω): S₀(ω + η) = S₀ω + S₀η and S₀(a • ω) = a·S₀ω.

subproblems.title: Currents annihilate test forms supported off their support
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P, every current T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n and every test form ω ∈ TestFormOn U n (C^∞, compact support, tsupport ω ⊆ U): if tsupport ω is disjoint from spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T) (zeroRegion(T) = union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T(η) = 0 for every test form η with tsupport η ⊆ W), then T(ω) = 0.

Source: the parenthetical argument in Step 1 of the parent proof ("a test form supported in the open zero region is annihilated: cover its compact support by finitely many open sets on which T vanishes and use a partition of unity"), with Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T), written out for the exact SimonGMT definitions.

Notation. For T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, `T.VanishesOn W` means T(η) = 0 for every η ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport η ⊆ W. Let 𝒲 be the family of all W ⊆ ℝ^P with W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W. By definition T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲 and T.support = U ∖ T.zeroRegion.

1. Let K := tsupport ω. Since ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, ω is C^∞, has compact support (so K is compact, in particular closed) and K ⊆ U.
2. K ⊆ ⋃𝒲. Let x ∈ K. Then x ∈ U, and x ∉ T.support by the disjointness hypothesis, i.e. x ∉ U ∖ T.zeroRegion; hence x ∈ T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲.
3. Every member of 𝒲 is open, so by compactness of K there are finitely many W_1, …, W_r ∈ 𝒲 (r ≥ 0; r = 0 when K = ∅) with K ⊆ W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_r (e.g. `IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover_image`; it is convenient to index the cover by the resulting finite subfamily rather than by Fin r).
4. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), with the model with corners 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), is a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, σ-compact smooth manifold, and K is closed and covered by the open sets W_i (i ranging over the finite index set of step 3). Hence there is a smooth partition of unity on K subordinate to (W_i): C^∞ functions ψ_1, …, ψ_r : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for every i and Σ_i ψ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∈ K (Mathlib `SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate`; a real-valued `ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P) 𝓘(ℝ)` function of class C^∞ is `ContDiff ℝ ∞` by `contMDiff_iff_contDiff`).
5. For each i put η_i(x) := ψ_i(x) • ω(x). Then η_i is C^∞ (a C^∞ scalar function times a C^∞ form). If ω(x) = 0 or ψ_i(x) = 0 then η_i(x) = 0, so support η_i ⊆ support ω ∩ support ψ_i; taking closures, tsupport η_i ⊆ K ∩ tsupport ψ_i ⊆ U ∩ W_i. In particular η_i has compact support (closed subset of the compact K). Thus η_i ∈ TestFormOn U n and tsupport η_i ⊆ W_i.
6. Since W_i ∈ 𝒲, T vanishes on W_i, so T(η_i) = 0 for every i.
7. ω = Σ_i η_i in TestFormOn U n (checked pointwise). If x ∈ K, then Σ_i ψ_i(x) • ω(x) = (Σ_i ψ_i(x)) • ω(x) = ω(x). If x ∉ K, then x ∉ support ω, so ω(x) = 0 and every η_i(x) = 0. (If r = 0 then K = ∅, ω = 0 and both sides are 0.)
8. T acts ℝ-linearly on TestFormOn U n (T.toCurrent is a linear map), so by steps 6 and 7, T(ω) = Σ_i T(η_i) = 0.
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of U disjoint from spt T, hence contained in the zero region, i.e. covered by the open sets W on which T vanishes.
Extract a finite subcover W_1, …, W_r of tsupport ω.
Take a smooth partition of unity ψ_1, …, ψ_r on tsupport ω subordinate to the W_i (Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate).
Each ψ_i • ω is a test form in U with tsupport in W_i, so T(ψ_i • ω) = 0.
ω = Σ_i ψ_i • ω pointwise, so T(ω) = 0 by linearity.

subproblems.title: Supports of boundaries, weak limits and linear combinations
subproblems.statement: (1) For P, m ∈ ℕ, any U ⊆ ℝ^P and Z ∈ D_{m+1}(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U (m+1)): spt ∂Z ⊆ spt Z. (2) For P, n ∈ ℕ, open U ⊆ ℝ^P, closed K ⊆ ℝ^P and Z_j, Z ∈ D_n(U) with spt Z_j ⊆ K for all j and Z_j ⇀ Z: spt Z ⊆ K. (3) For P, n ∈ ℕ, open U ⊆ ℝ^P, Z_1, Z_2, Z ∈ D_n(U) and a, b ∈ ℝ with Z(ω) = a·Z_1(ω) + b·Z_2(ω) for all ω ∈ D^n(U): spt Z ⊆ spt Z_1 ∪ spt Z_2.

Recall spt Z = U ∖ zeroRegion(Z), where zeroRegion(Z) is the union of all W with W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and Z(η) = 0 for every η ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (“Z vanishes on W”). (F2′): by the reused lemma isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support, Z(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ spt Z = ∅. (Balls): for x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, W := B_r(x) is open, closure W = B̄_r(x) (`closure_ball`) is compact (`isCompact_closedBall`); so W is admissible for zeroRegion as soon as B̄_r(x) ⊆ U and Z vanishes on W.

1. (Part (1).) Let x ∈ spt ∂Z, so x ∈ U, and suppose x ∉ spt Z. Then x ∈ zeroRegion(Z): x ∈ W for some W open with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, and Z vanishing on W. For φ ∈ D^m(U) with tsupport φ ⊆ W we have tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ W (SimonGMT `tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset`), so ∂Z(φ) = Z(dφ) = 0. Thus ∂Z vanishes on W, W is admissible for zeroRegion(∂Z), and x ∈ zeroRegion(∂Z), contradicting x ∈ spt ∂Z. Hence spt ∂Z ⊆ spt Z. (No openness of U is needed.)
2. (Part (2).) Let x ∈ spt Z ⊆ U and suppose x ∉ K. The set U ∖ K is open (U open, K closed) and contains x, so there is r > 0 with B̄_r(x) ⊆ U ∖ K (take half of a radius of a ball inside U ∖ K). Let W := B_r(x). For ω ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W: tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅, hence tsupport ω ∩ spt Z_j = ∅ for every j, so Z_j(ω) = 0 by (F2′); since Z_j(ω) → Z(ω) and limits in ℝ are unique, Z(ω) = 0. So Z vanishes on W, W is admissible, x ∈ zeroRegion(Z), contradicting x ∈ spt Z. Hence spt Z ⊆ K.
3. (Part (3).) Let x ∈ spt Z ⊆ U and suppose x ∉ spt Z_1 ∪ spt Z_2. As x ∈ U, x ∈ zeroRegion(Z_1) ∩ zeroRegion(Z_2) ∩ U, an open set (zero regions are unions of open sets, U is open), so there is r > 0 with B̄_r(x) contained in it. Let W := B_r(x). For ω ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W: tsupport ω ⊆ zeroRegion(Z_i), which is disjoint from spt Z_i = U ∖ zeroRegion(Z_i), so Z_i(ω) = 0 by (F2′) (i = 1, 2), and Z(ω) = a·0 + b·0 = 0. So Z vanishes on W, W is admissible (B̄_r(x) ⊆ U), x ∈ zeroRegion(Z), contradicting x ∈ spt Z. Hence spt Z ⊆ spt Z_1 ∪ spt Z_2. ∎
proof_key_steps: If Z vanishes on an admissible W then so does ∂Z, because tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ; hence spt ∂Z ⊆ spt Z.
For x ∉ K a small ball W around x misses K, so every Z_j kills test forms supported in W (reused vanishing lemma) and so does the weak limit Z.
For x outside spt Z_1 ∪ spt Z_2 a small ball lies in both zero regions; both Z_i, hence Z = aZ_1 + bZ_2, vanish on it.
